issues.body: SourceSegment still exposes declared_rows as an arbitrary usize. reconstruct_federated_public_inputs evaluates encoded_len for every source before check_shape; encoded_len uses unchecked additions and multiplications, so values near usize::MAX can panic in debug builds or wrap in release builds before Vec::with_capacity. Values that avoid arithmetic overflow still make encode loop over 0..declared_rows and append 96 bytes per padded row, enabling trivial memory/CPU exhaustion. The shape checks only compare caller-controlled values and do not establish that r belongs to a supported compiled scan circuit family.
issues.fix_hint: Validate declared_rows against the authoritative supported scan-circuit dimensions before any sizing or allocation, preferably by representing it with the same bounded circuit-dimension type. Use checked arithmetic for per-segment lengths and the aggregate capacity, returning MpcError on overflow. Add a negative test using an oversized value including usize::MAX that proves reconstruction returns MpcError without panic or allocation.
issues.title: Unbounded declared_rows still permits overflow and verifier resource exhaustion

verdict.summary: The round-6 major finding remains unresolved. SourceSegment::declared_rows is still an arbitrary usize, encoded_len still performs unchecked arithmetic, reconstruct_federated_public_inputs still sums encoded_len values before check_shape, and encode still iterates through every declared row. Thus malformed public input can panic or wrap during sizing and can force unbounded allocation/CPU work. No oversized-r negative test was added. Because the same major availability/correctness issue remains at the same severity, progress is stagnant.
